text.p: French shares were seen opening lower on Thursday following a 119.88 point drop on Wall Street, dealers said.
"Wall Street is going to knock the market down. We are close to the all-time high so it is a good time to take profits," said a dealer.
Credit Agricole said that the 2,907-2900 area was the main support zone with 2,922-17 as intermediate level.
Dealers said there were rumours of a big placement off-market in Alcatel Alsthom shares on Wednesday evening. Sources at Societe Generale denied that they placed the bank's 4.8 percent stake.

A spokesman at the SBF said the Paris Bourse had not been notified of a large off-market deal. Market participants do have some time to delare an off-market deal. Alcatel had no immediate comment on Wednesday.
* SEB reported a 17 percent rise in first half results on Wednesday which tradeers said was "pretty good".
* Eurotunnel is suspended pending its shareholders meeting today to vote on a debt restructuring plan.
* CGIP bought a 24 percent stake in Cap Gemini on Wednesday from DEBIS and placed 14 percent in the market, raising its stake to 30 percent from 20 percent.
* July CAC-40 futures were trading 17 points lower at 2,935. The CAC-40 index closed 0.71 percent higher at 2,950.56 on Wednesday.

* The previous government wanted to oust Rambaud and seize a nickel mine from the company to give it to a Kanak smelter project. New government said on Wednesday it supported a plan for a Kanak smelter but also wanted to keep the interests of company and minority shareholders in mind.

* Alcatel Alsthom is second biggest volume share, up 0.79 percent at 768 francs. There is a rumour that a big placement took place on Wednesday but Societe Generale source denies talk it sold the bank's 4.8 percent stake.
* Eurotunnel suspended pending shareholders meeting on debt conversion deal this afternoon.
